newsitem.title: CHINA: HK property stocks up after Hongkong Land news.
newsitem.headline: HK property stocks up after Hongkong Land news.

text.p: Hong Kong property stocks rose on demand for laggards, aided by news that Cheung Kong group had bought shares of Jardine Matheson Ltd and Hongkong Land Holdings Ltd, brokers said on Wednesday.
"The Hongkong Land news aided demand for property stocks, a sector which had lagged behind the market compared with the others," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas Securities.
Brokers said Hongkong Land held quality office property in Central in Hong Kong, and Cheung Kong group's buy-in into the company might boost investor confidence in office property.

Jardine Matheson announced on Tuesday that Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd and Hutchison Whampoa Ltd together held a 3.03 percent stake in Jardine Matheson and a 3.06 percent stake in Hongkong Land as of August 1.

"Expectations that Cheung Kong shares may follow Sun Hung Kai Properties testing an upside at HK$100, also fueled demand for Cheung Kong shares," said Ricky Tam, senior analyst at Delta Asia Securities.
Tam said the recent warm flats sale response also helped boost demand for property stocks.
Cheung Kong rose HK$4.25 or 4.86 percent to HK$91.75 at midday and Hutchison was up HK$3.00 to HK$81.75.
Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$1.00 to HK$106.50, New World Development Co Ltd gained HK$1.50 to HK$57.50, and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd rose HK$1.75 to HK$75.75.
